transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Aurora Tech), Liam O'Connor (Aurora Tech), Marta Ruiz (Aurora Tech), Speaker 5

Summary: quick console walkthrough showing per-route dashboards and cost breakdowns; demo of how Optimize suggests batching/quantization for cost-savings. Customer asked about dedicated capacity and KMS.

[00:00] Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Sophie, I'm the AE working with Aurora, and with me is Daniel from the SE team. How's everybody doing?
[00:07] Priya: Doing well, thanks Sophie. Excited to see the console. We've got a few folks on who care about cost and security.
[00:12] Daniel: Awesome. Quick agenda: we'll show the usage analytics, per-route dashboards, then the cost breakdown view and some Optimize recommendations. We'll leave time for Q&A.
[00:22] Liam: Sounds good. For context, we're running inference through our own API gateway on GKE, and we're exploring Dedicated vs Hosted — latency is important for some routes, cost for others.
[00:32] Sophie: Perfect, that's exactly what this part of the console tries to help with. I'll share my screen — bear with me if the screen share lags a bit.
[00:40] [screen share starts]
[01:05] Daniel: So the home dashboard shows token usage over time, broken down by model and route. Here's an example from a customer: you can see route A — high QPS but mostly short prompts — and route B — lower QPS but long context. Each line links to a per-route dashboard.
[01:26] Priya: Quick question — are these token counts pre- or post-caching? Like, if we have prefix caching, how does that show?
[01:35] Daniel: Good call. The default view shows billed tokens. We also have a cache hit metric; if the KV cache served X% of requests, billed tokens are lower. There can be slight mismatches if you enable prefix-ing caching, and sometimes the transcriber calls it key-v cache but it's KV cache.
[01:50] Marta: From a security perspective, can the console show which tokens were processed in our VPC or Dedicated hosts versus the hosted pool? We need that for audits.
[02:00] Sophie: Yes — per-route you can filter by deployment type. We surface an environment tag and export a CSV for audits. We'll include that in the security pack.
[02:12] Liam: Walk me through cost attribution — does it show per-route cost including GPU time, batching overhead, etc?
[02:20] Daniel: It breaks down costs to the per-token unit and infrastructure. The cost view has columns for raw token cost, batching efficiency, and kv cache savings. A lot of customers use the per-route 'cost per successful response' metric.
[02:35] Priya: You mentioned Optimize recommendations earlier — can it suggest batching or quantization?
[02:40] Daniel: Yep. We run an analysis on your route's latency and token distribution and suggest batching window sizes and quantization profiles. For example, it might recommend int8 quantization on route B because it has mostly long sequences and is tolerant to slight quality shifts. We also show expected cost delta and estimated impact on p95 latency.
[02:58] Priya: Is there any automation to roll that out? We don't want to manually tune every route.
[03:04] Daniel: We have a rollout feature — canary first, then full. It integrates with our rollout policies in the Console. You can set thresholds for quality regression and automatic rollback.
[03:18] Sophie: I'll jump to a worked example: here is a per-route dashboard for 'Search API' — top. It shows tokens, requests, avg tokens/request, p50/p95 latency, and cost. You can slice by model and time window.
[03:36] Liam: The p95 looks a little high on the 2pm spike — is that from cold-starts or scheduling?
[03:42] Daniel: Could be batching waits or autoscaler spin-up. For Dedicated pools we aim to eliminate cold GPU spin-ups; hosted may see higher variability depending on region and capacity.
[03:55] Marta: Regarding compliance, does Redwood support customer-managed KMS and HSM for keys? Our legal requires that.
[04:02] Sophie: Yes, for Private deployments and Dedicated we support KMS integrations and can surface logs for key usage. For hosted customers we offer managed KMS but we also have a bring-your-own-key option for certain enterprise tiers. We'll send the SOC2 doc and KMS integration guide after the call.
[04:18] Priya: Good. One other thing — are we able to tag requests from our app so the console can map cost back to internal teams?
[04:25] Daniel: Absolutely. The request metadata can include a route tag, team tag, or customer id, and the per-route view aggregates by those tags.
[04:32] [05:00] Daniel: Now, diving into cost breakdown: here's the per-token cost estimate. Note that batching reduces per-token overhead; the console simulates batching windows and shows theoretical savings. For instance, a 50ms batching window saved 18% on this customer's text-gen route.
[05:18] Priya: How accurate are those simulations compared to real-world? I mean, we can't risk degrading p95.
[05:25] Daniel: The simulator uses your observed arrival distribution to model latency. We also recommend running a short pilot where we actually route a subset through the Dedicated pool to observe real metrics before broad rollouts.
[05:36] Sophie: That pilot is usually 1-2 hours at production traffic or scaled-down but representative. We'll collaborate on the test script.
[05:45] Liam: On the Dedicated side, what's the contract model? Monthly reserved capacity?
[05:50] Sophie: Yes, Dedicated is reserved GPU capacity with monthly or annual commits. You can also configure burst pools and autoscaling policies. Pricing varies by region and GPU type — we'll include a couple of example quote tiers in the follow-up.
[06:05] Marta: For the pilot and any dedicated deployment, we need audit logs and retention options. What's standard?
[06:12] Daniel: We store request logs for X days by default and have extended retention as an add-on. Logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export. We'll include the exact retention numbers in the security doc; I think the transcriber occasionally said 'SAML and RBAC' funny earlier but yes we support SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC.
[06:32] [07:00] Priya: Ok let's talk concrete numbers — if we had 10k qps on route A with avg 30 tokens, what's the per-route monthly cost ballpark?
[07:11] Sophie: We can ballpark with a couple assumptions, but given the variability we prefer to run a short benchmark with your exact model and sequence length. For a rough estimate, the console's cost simulator will give you a projected monthly spend; we'll send an exported CSV with examples after the call.
[07:28] Priya: Cool. Another concern — model variants and fallbacks. If Dedicated pool is constrained, can traffic fall back to hosted instances?
[07:36] Daniel: Yes, the smart routing supports fallback to hosted or alternate model variants. Policies are configurable per-route so you can set strict or lenient fallbacks.
[07:48] Liam: About monitoring: do we get per-token breakdown so we can attribute to features? We want to tie cost to product metrics.
[07:55] Daniel: The per-route dashboard links to per-feature tags; you can export the cost by tag and join it to product analytics. Many customers push tags automatically from their API gateway.
[08:10] [10:00] Sophie: We'll capture next steps live: (1) Sophie to send pricing and example quotes, (2) Daniel to draft pilot plan, (3) Aurora to provide traffic profile and compliance questions.
[08:30] Priya: That works. We also want a sample of the per-route dashboard export so our finance folks can review.
[08:36] Sophie: We'll send a sample CSV.
[08:40] Marta: Quick nit — your docs sometimes mention 'Redwood Dedicated' and 'Redwood Private' interchangeably; can you send a one-pager clarifying which features live where?
[08:48] Daniel: Yep, we'll include a deployment matrix that maps features (KMS, Audit logs, Burst pools) to Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
[09:00] Priya: If we go forward with a pilot, what's the timeline to spin up a dedicated pool in our region?
[09:07] Sophie: Typically 1-2 weeks after contract for dedicated reserved capacity; pilot on hosted or a temporary dedicated pool we can get started in 2-3 days for a short run, depending on region.
[09:21] Liam: For the pilot, we'd want to run our main model and also a reranking flow — rerankers are latency-sensitive. Can the console correlate reranker calls separately?
[09:31] Daniel: Yes, you can define separate routes, and the per-route dashboard will show p50/p95 and cost breakdown for each. Rerankers often benefit from smaller batching windows.
[09:45] [20:00] Sophie: jumping ahead to Optimize: here's a sample recommendation. For route B we suggested int8_q4 on the model and a 30ms batching window. Expected cost delta: -26%, expected p95 impact: +6ms.
[20:22] Priya: How do you validate quality? We have a strict eval set for our assistants.
[20:28] Daniel: Optimize can run evals tied to your prompt sets. We can gate rollouts on a quality threshold; if scored quality drops we auto-rollback.
[20:40] Priya: Excellent. That was a big worry.
[20:45] Sophie: Anything else from the team?
[20:48] Marta: Please include details on network egress and data residency in the follow-up.
[20:52] Sophie: Noted.
[21:00] Priya: I'll share traffic slices and the eval set offline.
[21:04] Sophie: Great. We'll follow up with the docs and pilot plan. Thanks everyone.
[44:10] [call ends]

Notes: occasional transcription noise — speaker 5 was on the call but didn't speak much; some product names are colloquially referred to (e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' vs 'Private deploy'). Agreed items: pricing, security docs, pilot with test script.
